review.summary: The Phoenix proposal has been rejected for production promotion due to several areas of attention and a blocked promotion gate. Key technical concerns include the need for improved container hardening and dependency reproducibility.
top_technical_reasons: Container hardening requires attention to ensure security.
Dependency reproducibility is flagged for attention, indicating potential issues with consistent builds.
The fixed 24-month promotion gate is blocked, preventing advancement to production.
review.candidate_safety: The candidate has not demonstrated sufficient safety and reliability to meet production standards.

next_experiments.hypothesis: Improving container hardening will enhance security.
next_experiments.change: Implement a non-root Docker user and health checks.
next_experiments.why_it_is_informative: This will provide insights into the security posture of the deployment environment.

next_experiments.hypothesis: Enhancing dependency reproducibility will lead to more stable builds.
next_experiments.change: Pin runtime dependencies and implement dependency vulnerability scanning.
next_experiments.metric_gate: Reduction in build failures due to dependency issues.
next_experiments.why_it_is_informative: This will help assess the impact of dependency management on overall system stability.

next_experiments.hypothesis: Establishing artifact retention and rollback policies will improve deployment safety.

next_experiments.metric_gate: Successful execution of rollback scenarios without failures.
next_experiments.why_it_is_informative: This will evaluate the effectiveness of the rollback process in maintaining system integrity.
